slides.0.title: Key Red Grape Varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Xinomavro and Agiorgitiko
slides.1.title: The two pillars of Greek red
slides.1.highlights.0.title: North: Xinomavro
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Centred on Naoussa; high tannin and acidity, can age over a decade, often compared with Nebbiolo
slides.1.highlights.1.title: South: Agiorgitiko
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The signature of Nemea, where the PDO requires 100%; Greece's most planted red as of 2012
slides.1.content: Grasp the "north Xinomavro / south Agiorgitiko" spine first, then add the others.
slides.2.title: Xinomavro in depth
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Pale colour, quick to turn brick
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The colour is not deep; turning brick-red with age is typical
slides.2.highlights.1.title: High tannin and acid
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A firm structure that needs time or careful winemaking to soften
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Key appellations
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Naoussa, Amyndeo, Goumenissa and Slopes of Meliton (northern Macedonia)
slides.2.content: Comparison with Nebbiolo is a common Diploma theme: both are high in acid and tannin, pale and long-lived.
slides.3.title: Agiorgitiko and other reds
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Agiorgitiko
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A wide range: rosé, light young reds, and structured oak-aged wines
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Mavrodaphne
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Around Patras; closely tied to sweet fortified wine (covered in Level 2)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Mandilaria
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Deeply coloured and tannic, common on the Aegean islands and Crete
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Limnio, Mavrotragano and Kotsifali
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Limnio (Lemnos, mentioned by Aristotle); Mavrotragano (Santorini, concentrated dark fruit); Kotsifali (Crete)
slides.3.content: Limniona (Thessaly) is also an important regional red; we cover it with Thessaly in Level 2.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which Greek red is often compared with Nebbiolo?
Xinomavro is pale, high in acid and tannin and ageworthy, like Nebbiolo.
Which grape (100%) does the Nemea PDO require?
Nemea is the home of Agiorgitiko.
Which place is Mavrotragano mainly linked to?
Mavrotragano is a dark red variety revived on Santorini.
